RFC8907-10-1.note: {single-polarity} on the row: no configuration enables the flag. (a) forbidden: any configuration state, including a keyless server, under which the client sends with TAC_PLUS_UNENCRYPTED_FLAG. (b) TestRFC8907UnencryptedModeIsNotReachableFromConfiguration reads the socket: a keyed config puts wire[3]&0x01 == 0 (assert.Zero), a keyless config writes no bytes (assert.Empty); TestRFC8907ClientNeverSendsUnobfuscatedBody requires the wire body to be the pseudo-pad XOR of the plaintext.

RFC8907-10-2.note: (a) forbidden: a client request whose flags octet has 0x01 set, or a send with no key. (b) TestRFC8907ClientNeverSendsUnobfuscatedBody fails when wire[3]&FlagUnencrypted != 0 and requires the body to decode through the pad; TestPacketMarshalNoEncryption requires ErrNoSharedSecret for nil and empty keys with zero bytes written; TestRFC8907BuildRejectsMissingSecret requires Build to refuse a keyless server with ErrNoSharedSecret and no authenticator.

RFC8907-10.5.1-1.note: (a) forbidden: exposing the shared secret in display, diagnostics, logs or accounting records. (b) TestRFC8907SharedSecretConfigBuildAndDisplay asserts the display tree masks the key while the live key still decodes a real exchange; TestRFC8907SharedSecretDiagnosticRedaction fails on the key, its base64 or byte list in fmt, %#v, JSON and slog output; TestRFC8907SharedSecretCommandRedaction fails on secret words in DisplayCommand; TestRFC8907AccountingRedactsConfigSecretWithoutChangingExecution asserts accounting tokens carry the placeholder.

RFC8907-10.5.1-2.note: (a) forbidden: rejecting or truncating a shared key of 32 characters or more. (b) TestRFC8907LongSharedKeysAuthenticate completes a PASS exchange with 32- and 300-character keys; TestRFC8907SharedKeyIsNotTruncated asserts the pad for 32 characters differs from the pad for the first 31; TestRFC8907SharedSecretConfigBuildAndDisplay drives a 32-character key through Build into a real accounting exchange.

RFC8907-10.5.2-1.note: TestRFC8907ClientRefusesUnobfuscatedReply asserts only the FAIL status for an authentication session; the MUST close the TCP session clause is not asserted, and the authorization-session FAIL path is not exercised

RFC8907-10.5.4-1.note: (a) forbidden: Ze interpreting a shared argument-value pair differently from its defined meaning. (b) TestRFC8907MandatoryCommandPolicyAccepted asserts an exact service/cmd/cmd-arg policy with separators inside the value is enacted, which is one consistent-interpretation case. The negatives (TestRFC8907MandatoryCommandPolicyDenied, TestRFC8907MandatorySessionPolicyDenied) prove the next sentence of Section 10.5.4, unrecognized mandatory argument evaluated as FAIL, which RFC8907-6-1 carries. No assertion covers interpretation of the rest of the base dictionary Ze consumes (priv-lvl is asserted under RFC8907-8.1-1 only).

RFC8907-3.7-1.note: (a) forbidden: a username sent without UsernameCasePreserved enforcement: no width mapping, no NFC, case folded, or a PRECIS-disallowed string (control, private use, ZWJ outside context, invalid UTF-8, bidi-rule violation) sent. (b) TestRFC8907UsernameProfileOnWire reads the username off the wire for all three services and requires "Ａlice\u0301" to arrive as "Alicé" (width-mapped, NFC, case kept); TestRFC8907ForbiddenUsernameNeverSent requires errRequestInvalid and no server contact for "alice\x00", "alice\ue000", "a\u200db", "\xff" and "\u05d0a" on every service.

RFC8907-3.7-2.note: Clause 'all other text fields' is proven for four fields only: TestRFC8907NonPrintableTextRejected fails on a control, DEL or non-ASCII byte in the PAP password (authen data), an authorization cmd argument, the accounting port, and an authentication server_msg; TestRFC8907PrintableTextRoundTrip is the positive. validateText also guards rem_addr (authen.go:66, author.go:55, acct.go:62), the authentication and authorization port (authen.go:63, author.go:52), accounting arguments (acct.go:78) and the authorization/accounting reply message (reply.go:60,66); removing any of those calls leaves every tagged assertion green.

RFC8907-4-1.note: validateResponseHeader compares the reply major nibble with the request, not with 0xc, and the test server echoes the request version: a client emitting major 0xD stays green in both TestTacacsClientAuthenticatePass and the wrong-major-version case; no tagged unit asserts the emitted major version is 0xc

RFC8907-4-2.note: tests assert reply seq == request seq+1 only; the echoing test server hides the client parity (a client sending seq 2 would get 3 and pass), and the seq-7 negative is refused for not being seq+1, not for being odd from a server

RFC8907-4-3.note: TestRFC8907SessionIDComesFromCryptoRand substitutes crypto/rand.Reader and requires the id to be exactly those octets; TestRandomSessionIDDistinct adds cross-session distinctness

RFC8907-4-4.note: TestTacacsClientAuthenticatePass asserts only status and server_msg; the test server always echoes session_id, so removing the client mismatch guard or changing the id would stay green; single-polarity marker acknowledges no negative

RFC8907-4-5.note: TestPacketHeaderMarshalRoundTrip is a symmetric marshal/unmarshal round trip with no wire-octet assertion: a little-endian codec on both sides passes

RFC8907-4.1-1.note: Only the data field is asserted: TestRFC8907ZeroLengthDataIsReadAsAbsent (data_len 0 -> Empty) and TestRFC8907PresentZeroByteIsNotReadAsAbsent (one zero byte retained). The quote binds any variable-length field whose length is zero (server_msg, user, port, rem_addr, reply arguments); no tagged assertion goes red if another zero-length field were read as present or read past.

RFC8907-4.1-2.note: (a) forbidden: a session's first packet with a seq_no other than 1, or accepting a reply that does not follow it. (b) TestRFC8907FirstPacketCarriesSequenceOne requires requests[0].SeqNo == 1 on each new connection; TestRFC8907ReplyReusingSequenceOneIsRefused requires a reply carrying seq_no 1 to fail Authenticate and validateResponseHeader to report "sequence mismatch". The increment clause is descriptive ("will").

RFC8907-4.1-3.note: (a) forbidden: refusing a reply because undefined flag bits are set, or letting undefined bits mask a defined flag. (b) TestRFC8907UnknownHeaderFlagsIgnored sets reply flags 0xf2 (undefined bits only) and fails unless status == PASS with no error; TestRFC8907UnknownFlagsDoNotMaskDowngrade sets 0x81 and fails unless the result is FAIL. The SHOULD-zero-on-write half is not a MUST.

RFC8907-4.3-1.note: (a) forbidden: a second packet on a connection before the server echoed single-connect. (b) TestRFC8907NoSecondPacketWithoutSingleConnect (no echo) requires two connections and requestsOn(0) of length 1; TestRFC8907SecondSessionReusesEstablishedConnection (echo) requires one connection carrying two requests.

RFC8907-4.3-2.note: (a) forbidden: acting on the single-connect flag after the second packet, by leaving the pool when a later reply clears it or by re-signalling it. (b) TestRFC8907FlagClearedOnLaterReplyIsIgnored requires one connection carrying three requests although replies after the first clear the flag; TestRFC8907ClientDoesNotResignalSingleConnect requires requests[1].Flags and requests[2].Flags == 0.

RFC8907-4.3-3.note: (a) forbidden: failing a later session, or writing to the dead socket, after the server closed an established single-connect TCP. TestRFC8907ServerClosureOfPooledConnectionIsAccommodated goes red on that (authenticatePass, require.Len connections 2, requestsOn(1) 1). The negative-tagged TestRFC8907ClosureOnFreshDialIsNotRetried asserts a neighbouring property (a closure on a fresh dial is not retried), which does not violate this requirement, and the row carries no {single-polarity} marker, so only one genuine polarity exists.

RFC8907-4.4-1.note: (a) forbidden: applying an ERROR reply as a result (terminal rejection) instead of behaving as if the server were unreachable. (b) TestRFC8907ErrorUsesBackupServer fails for authentication, authorization and accounting unless the backup is contacted and its status 1 is returned with no error; TestRFC8907FailDoesNotUseBackupServer is the discriminating pair: a FAIL keeps failStatus and never contacts the backup.

RFC8907-4.4-2.note: (a) forbidden: a new session on a single-connect connection after a reply on it failed validation. (b) TestRFC8907NoNewSessionOnBrokenPooledConnection (session_id corrupted on the second reply) requires two connections and requestsOn(0) of length 2, so a third request on the broken TCP goes red; TestRFC8907HealthyPooledConnectionKeepsAcceptingSessions requires one connection carrying three requests.

RFC8907-4.4-3.note: (a) forbidden: leaving the broken single-connect connection open. (b) TestRFC8907BrokenPooledConnectionIsClosed requires waitClosed on the server side of the broken TCP; TestRFC8907HealthyPooledConnectionStaysOpen requires isClosed false after three healthy sessions.

RFC8907-4.6-1.note: Clause 'the sum is not identical' has two directions. TestRFC8907TrailingReplyBytesRejected proves only sum < datalength (one trailing decrypted byte -> error, status 0) for all three services, and TestRFC8907ExactReplyLengthsAccepted is the positive. No tagged unit sends component lengths whose sum exceeds datalength, so the other half of the inequality (reply.go:56 total != len(body), and the earlier truncation guards) is unasserted.

RFC8907-5.1-1.note: (a) forbidden: a START with no username whose user_len is not 0. (b) TestRFC8907AuthenStartAbsentUserWritesZeroLength requires body[4] == 0, no user bytes and the port at offset 8; TestRFC8907AuthenStartPresentUserWritesItsLength requires body[4] == len("alice") and the user bytes.

RFC8907-5.4.2.2-1.note: (a) forbidden: a PAP login with more than one START/REPLY, including a CONTINUE. (b) TestRFC8907PAPExchangeIsOneStartOneReply requires exactly one authentication request on the connection; TestRFC8907PAPClientSendsNoContinue replies GETPASS and requires an error, a nil reply and requestsOn(0) of length 1.

RFC8907-5.4.2.2-2.note: Clause 'MUST contain a username' has no red assertion in a tagged unit: TestRFC8907PAPStartCarriesUserAndPassword asserts the user and data fields when a username is given, and the absent-username refusal lives only in the untagged TestRFC8907PAPRequiresPresentBoundedUsername. TestRFC8907PAPStartRefusesPasswordItCannotCarry proves a length bound, not presence of the password. The data-field-is-the-password clause is enforced.

RFC8907-5.4.2.6-2.note: Clause 1 ('MUST be set to TAC_PLUS_AUTHEN_SVC_ENABLE when requesting an ENABLE') has no assertion and no annotation: Ze sets only authenServiceLogin (authen.go:176) and never requests ENABLE, but the row carries no {single-polarity} or {not-applicable} argument for that half. Clause 2 is covered, though the two tagged units are one assertion wearing two hats (Equal LOGIN implies NotEqual ENABLE).

RFC8907-5.4.3-1.note: (a) forbidden: processing RESTART as anything but FAIL. (b) TestRFC8907RestartIsProcessedAsFail requires ErrorIs aaa.ErrAuthRejected, Authenticated false and Source == backendName; TestRFC8907ErrorIsNotProcessedAsFail is the discriminating pair: ERROR must not be ErrAuthRejected.

RFC8907-6-1.note: (a) forbidden: authorizing when a mandatory argument cannot be handled. (b) TestRFC8907MandatoryCommandPolicyDenied fails if an unsupported mandatory argument or value grants the command or consults the local fallback; TestRFC8907MandatorySessionPolicyDenied fails if session login grants profiles under an unenforceable mandatory argument; positives TestRFC8907MandatoryCommandPolicyAccepted (recognized mandatory values authorize) and TestRFC8907OptionalCommandPolicyIgnored (unsupported optional is disregarded).

RFC8907-6.1-1.note: (a) forbidden: a user_len that is not the BYTE length of the user field (for example a character count). Both tagged units use ASCII users, where bytes and characters coincide: TestRFC8907AuthorRequestUserLenMatchesUser asserts body[4] == 5 and the five user bytes for "alice", and TestRFC8907AuthorRequestRefusesUserItCannotMeasure asserts a 256-byte ASCII user is refused. A user_len computed as a rune count stays green; the multi-byte case ("Alicé") is asserted only in TestRFC8907UsernameProfileOnWire, tagged to RFC8907-3.7-1.

RFC8907-6.1-2.note: (a) forbidden: an argument whose name contains = or *. (b) TestRFC8907ArgumentNamesCarryNoSeparator requires every built name to be service, cmd or cmd-arg; TestRFC8907ArgumentValueKeepsSeparatorOutOfName requires splitTacacsArgs("set key=a*b value=*") to equal exactly service=shell, cmd=set, cmd-arg=key=a*b, cmd-arg=value=*, so a token carried as a name goes red.

RFC8907-6.2-1.note: (a) forbidden: under PASS_ADD, dropping the requested arguments or not applying the returned ones. (b) TestRFC8907PassAddRetainsCommand fails if the requested command is lost; TestRFC8907PassAddCannotIgnoreCommandExtension fails if an added mandatory cmd-arg is ignored or falls back to local policy; TestRFC8907SessionPrivilegeApplied fails unless the returned priv-lvl selects its mapped profile.

RFC8907-6.2-2.note: (a) forbidden: under PASS_REPL, using the request arguments instead of the reply ones. (b) TestRFC8907PassReplCannotAuthorizeOriginalCommand fails if an empty, incomplete, changed, reordered or re-split replacement authorizes the original command or consults the local fallback; TestRFC8907IncompleteSessionReplacementDenied fails if session replacement inherits service/cmd from the request; positives TestRFC8907PassReplPreservesExactCommand and TestRFC8907SessionReplacementMapsZero (reply priv-lvl 0 applied).

RFC8907-6.2-3.note: (a) forbidden: allowing a request the server answered with FAIL. (b) TestRFC8907AuthorizationFailDenies requires Authorize false and zero calls to a permissive local policy; TestRFC8907AuthorizationPassAddIsNotDenied requires PASS_ADD to allow.

RFC8907-7-1.note: producer (acct.go flag switch) allowlists START, STOP, WATCHDOG and WATCHDOG|START, but the tagged units probe only the 0x01 bit; a denylist of 0x01 alone would pass, and bits 0x10-0x80 are never exercised

RFC8907-7-2.note: (a) forbidden: a request carrying START and STOP together. (b) TestRFC8907AccountingStartStopCombinationRefused requires errors.Is(err, errRequestInvalid) for Flags START|STOP; TestAcctRequestMarshalStartStop marshals START and STOP as separate flags.

RFC8907-7.2-1.note: (a) forbidden: STOP with WATCHDOG set. (b) TestRFC8907AccountingStopWatchdogCombinationRefused requires errRequestInvalid for STOP|WATCHDOG; TestRFC8907StopRecordNeverCarriesWatchdog requires Flags&WATCHDOG == 0 on the queued STOP; TestRFC8907StopRecordCarriesStopFlagOnly requires Flags == STOP.

RFC8907-8-1.note: The quote binds every use case the Section 8 dictionary serves. The tagged units assert only command accounting: TestRFC8907CommandRecordsUseDictionaryArguments requires service/cmd/cmd-arg/task_id/start_time|stop_time and TestRFC8907CommandRecordsCarryNoForeignArgument refuses names outside the dictionary. Authorization requests (command and session) are not asserted under this row, and the 8.2 rows that carry them are themselves weak.

RFC8907-8.1-1.note: (a) forbidden: processing a numeric argument whose length Ze cannot accommodate, or not applying Section 6.1 to it. (b) TestRFC8907InvalidMandatoryPrivilegeDenied asserts ErrAuthRejected and zero profiles for priv-lvl=18446744073709551631 and a 242-digit value (mandatory -> authorization failed); TestRFC8907OverlongOptionalPrivilegeCannotElevate asserts the overlong optional priv-lvl is disregarded (profile ops); TestRFC8907SessionPrivilegeApplied is the positive (priv-lvl=15 -> admin). priv-lvl is the only numeric argument Ze processes; timeout and others are refused as unsupported mandatory.

RFC8907-8.1-2.note: (a) forbidden: an absolute date/time in local time, or not in epoch seconds, without a timezone argument. (b) TestRFC8907StartTimeIsEpochSeconds bounds start_time to time.Now().Unix(); TestRFC8907StartTimeIgnoresLocalZone sets time.Local five hours east and asserts no shift and no timezone argument. stop_time, the other absolute date/time Ze emits (accounting.go line 189), has no assertion, so a local-zone stop_time passes.

RFC8907-8.2-1.note: (a) forbidden: an authorization or accounting request without a service argument. (b) TestRFC8907ServiceArgumentAlwaysFirst and TestRFC8907ServiceArgumentPresentForEmptyCommand assert service=shell only for splitTacacsArgs, the command-authorization builder. The session authorization request built in authenticator.go (args service=shell, cmd=) and the accounting records have no assertion in a unit tagged to this row, so "always" is proven for one request kind.

RFC8907-8.2-2.note: (a) forbidden: a service=shell request without a cmd argument. (b) TestRFC8907CmdArgumentFollowsShellService and TestRFC8907CmdArgumentPresentForEmptyCommand assert cmd= after service=shell only for splitTacacsArgs. The session authorization request (authenticator.go, service=shell with cmd=) is not asserted by a unit tagged to this row.

RFC8907-8.3-1.note: (a) forbidden: a Section 8.2 argument (service, cmd, cmd-arg) before task_id/start_time/stop_time in an accounting record. (b) TestRFC8907AccountingArgumentsPrecedeAuthorizationOnes asserts task_id and start_time (START) and task_id and stop_time (STOP) index below service; TestRFC8907NoAuthorizationArgumentPrecedesAccountingOne fails on any service/cmd/cmd-arg seen before task_id or start_time in START. Both records share accountingArguments.

RFC8907-8.3-2.note: (a) forbidden: START and STOP of one command with different task_id values. (b) TestRFC8907StartAndStopShareTaskID require.Equal(startID, stopID); TestRFC8907SecondCommandCarriesOtherTaskID require.NotEqual for a second command.

RFC8907-8.3-3.note: (a) forbidden: two active START records sharing a task_id, or a task_id reused in START before its STOP. (b) TestRFC8907ActiveTaskIDsAreDistinct fails on any repeat among sixteen START records with no STOP; TestRFC8907TaskIDNeverReappears asserts a used task_id never reappears in eight later STARTs.

RFC8907-8.3-4.note: (a) forbidden: an entered command with no accounting START, including a command authorization denied or that is unknown or malformed. (b) TestDispatcherAccountsRefusedCommands asserts starts == [input] for a denied, an unknown and a malformed command; TestRFC8907TypedDispatchAccountsDeniedCommand asserts START and STOP for a denied typed dispatch; api_test.go denied-stream and TACACS wire tests (rfc8907_dispatch_wire_test.go) assert real START packets; TestRFC8907AccountingRequiresDestination refuses accounting with no destination at Build.

RFC8907-8.3-5.note: (a) forbidden: a command accounting record without service or cmd, or dropping needed cmd-arg arguments. (b) TestRFC8907CommandRecordsCarryServiceCmdAndArgs asserts service=shell, cmd=show, cmd-arg=bgp, cmd-arg=summary in START and STOP; TestRFC8907EmptyCommandRecordStillCarriesServiceAndCmd asserts service=shell and cmd= for an empty command.

RFC8907-x-2.note: (a) forbidden: the client using the FOLLOW redirection, by contacting the named server or treating FOLLOW as success or fallback. (b) TestRFC8907FollowTargetIsNeverContacted fails if the FOLLOW target receives a connection; TestRFC8907FollowIsNotAuthenticated asserts ErrAuthRejected and not authenticated; TestRFC8907AuthorizationFollowDeniesWithoutFallback asserts denial with zero local fallback calls.
